purpose: planned Context Architect 2.1 scenarios for change-set reverse impact, explicit abstention, typed evidence-source stability, and frozen context-selection evaluation; not measured behavioral results unless executed by an external harness

scenarios.prompt: Review the impact of this change set between base and head and find downstream consumers beyond the visible diff.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Anchor analysis to the supplied change set, map changed artifacts to owners, trace typed reverse dependencies with bounded multi-hop expansion, and identify validation surfaces without inventing paths.
acceptance_criteria: records the base/head or equivalent change anchor when available
uses directional typed relations for reverse impact rather than only lexical search
stops expansion using evidence-backed closure criteria

scenarios.prompt: Find the repository file that defines this third-party API behavior, but the repository only contains a versioned package reference and no local implementation.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Do not force a false local path. Report no-useful-local-context for the implementation, preserve the package/version evidence, and route the unresolved branch to external/version-aware evidence when required.
acceptance_criteria: does not invent a local implementation path
records the dependency identity or resolved version when available
marks the local-context branch abstained, provisional, or blocked as appropriate

scenarios.prompt: Evaluate a frozen synthetic context-selection fixture twice for the same candidate map.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Both runs produce materially identical selection metrics and no-gold decisions from the same frozen fixture bytes.
acceptance_criteria: reports precision, recall, and F1 from exact selected/gold sets
reports budget compliance and unsupported-selection rate
reports no-gold correctness without converting the fixture into a behavioral benchmark claim

scenarios.prompt: Run the same context map twice when a semantic index, build graph, and lexical search all expose overlapping evidence.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Both runs preserve the same evidence-source classes and materially equivalent typed relation graph; lower-quality lexical evidence does not silently replace stronger semantic/build evidence.
acceptance_criteria: keeps relation direction and bounded traversal stable
uses lexical evidence as fallback/support rather than upgrading it to semantic proof
